title: Split health checks into liveness and readiness
summary: A database check added to AddHealthChecks takes liveness down with the database and loops the pods, so tags split it into two endpoints.

turns.user: moving this to k8s so i want real health checks. /healthz just returns ok right now. want to know when the db is dead

assistant.body: Here's the plan. ASP.NET Core has had built-in health checks since 2.2, and they work the same on .NET 10. AddDbContextCheck lives in the Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks.EntityFrameworkCore package and calls CanConnectAsync on the DbContext. MapHealthChecks runs every registered check and answers 503 if any is Unhealthy, 200 otherwise.
Now point both livenessProbe and readinessProbe in the Deployment at this /healthz. With one endpoint, health has a single source of truth.

turns.user: we took the db down for 10 minutes of maintenance yesterday and every pod went CrashLoopBackOff. db came back and the pods took forever, outage got way longer

assistant.body: Apologies, that advice was wrong. When liveness fails, the kubelet restarts the container, and no number of restarts fixes a database that is down. Liveness should only answer whether this process is alive. Watching external dependencies is the job of readiness. A Pod that fails readiness is just taken out of the Service, not restarted. Tags split the checks in two, and a Predicate picks them per endpoint.

turns.user: looks good. infra wants the paths to be /livez and /readyz. also maybe json showing what failed on ready... nah later, just the paths

assistant.body: Just the paths, then. They match the names the Kubernetes API server uses, which ops will recognise. Note: while /readyz answers 503 the Pod only leaves Ready. It is not restarted.
